# jtoken

> Compress JSON-shaped documents (plain JSON, MongoDB shell/Extended JSON, Elasticsearch hits) for LLM prompts: fewer tokens, readable line-oriented output, lossless round-trip, CLI, and tiktoken-based token measurement. Python 3.8+, MIT, stdlib-only core.

jtoken exists because retrieved JSON documents in RAG/agent prompts repeat syntactic keys and waste context-window tokens. jtoken rewrites those documents into a short line-oriented format and can decode back **exactly**, including Mongo `ObjectId`/`$date`/`$numberLong` forms and Elasticsearch hit envelopes, via a normalization context.

## API reference

### Core codec
- `jtoken.encode(data: dict) -> str` — compress a nested scalar dict into jtoken text.
- `jtoken.decode(text: str) -> dict` — reconstruct the nested dict.
- Aliases: `jtoken.dumps`, `jtoken.loads`.

### Document workflow (dialect-aware, lossless)
- `jtoken.encode_document(raw, *, source="auto", context=None) -> (text, NormalizationContext)`
  `source`/auto-detect accepts: `json`, `python`, `mongo_extended` (`$oid`, `$date`, `$numberLong`, …), `mongo_shell` (`ObjectId(...)`, `ISODate(...)`, `NumberLong(...)`), `elastic_hit` (`_source` envelope), `elastic_source`.
- `jtoken.decode_document(text, *, target="python", context) -> Any`
  `target` accepts: `python`, `json`, `mongo_extended`, `mongo_shell`, `elastic_hit`, `elastic_source`.
- `NormalizationContext` sidecar records list paths, dotted keys, ESL envelope metadata and BSON type markers (`object_id`, `datetime`, `datetime_long`, `long`); methods `to_dict()` / `from_dict()`. Pass `--context-out file` / `--context-in file` on the CLI.

### Token measurement
- `jtoken.count_tokens(data, *, model="cl100k_base", backend="auto|tiktoken|estimate") -> int`
- `jtoken.count_text_tokens(text, *, model="cl100k_base", backend="auto") -> int`
- `jtoken.token_savings(data, *, model, backend, json_indent=2) -> TokenSavings`
  `TokenSavings` fields: `jtoken_tokens`, `json_tokens`, `saved`, `percent`.

### CLI
```
jtoken encode --input-format mongo_shell -f doc.json --context-out doc.ctx.json
jtoken decode --output-format mongo_extended -f doc.jtoken --context-in doc.ctx.json
jtoken stats --backend tiktoken --model gpt-4o -f doc.json
jtoken count --backend estimate -f doc.json
```

## Encoding rules

- Nested dicts flatten with dot notation (`page.referrer: …`).
- Repeated booleans/nulls collapse: `trues: active, verified`, `nulls: ref`.
- Lists become indexed keys and are reconstructed from the context.
- Keys containing `.` are escaped and restored from the context.
- Reserved top-level keys: `nulls`, `trues`, `falses`. Keys cannot contain `": "` in the core codec.

## Measured performance (tiktoken cl100k_base, 50 docs each, all verified lossless)

| Payload | JSON (pretty) | jtoken | Saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Elasticsearch hits | 12,038 | 10,671 | 11.4% |
| MongoDB documents (extended JSON) | 9,437 | 7,630 | 19.1% |
| Nested API events | 12,773 | 11,083 | 13.2% |
| Total | 34,248 | 29,384 | 14.2% |

Savings are structure-dependent: repetitive machine-generated JSON compresses much better than prose-heavy documents. Reproduce: `python3 benchmarks/benchmark.py` (https://github.com/HermannSamimi/jtoken/blob/main/benchmarks/benchmark.py).

## LangChain integration

`langchain-jtoken` (https://pypi.org/project/langchain-jtoken/) provides `JSONTokenDocumentTransformer`, a LangChain `BaseDocumentTransformer` that compresses JSON `page_content` while preserving metadata; non-JSON content passes through unchanged.

```python
from langchain_jtoken import JSONTokenDocumentTransformer
docs = JSONTokenDocumentTransformer().transform_documents(docs)
```

## Common gotchas

- Lossless round-trip for dialect data requires keeping the context (sidecar or embedded header).
- Encoding collapses lists into indexed keys: use `decode_document` with the context to restore them as lists.
- Plain `jtoken.decode` targets JSON dicts; use `decode_document(..., target=...)` for Mongo/ES shapes.
